[47, 50]

Let $(Q,\tau)$ be a virtually acyclic $\imath$ quiver. Then there exists a $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{q})$ -algebra monomorphism $\widetilde{\psi}:\widetilde{\textbf{U}}^{\imath}_{|v=\sqrt{q}}\rightarrow{\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}(\mathbb{F}_{q}Q,\tau)},$ which sends

$\displaystyle B_{j}\mapsto\frac{-1}{q-1}[S_{j}],\text{ if }j\in\mathbb{I}_{\tau},$
$\displaystyle\qquad\qquad\widetilde{k}_{i}\mapsto-q^{-1}[\mathbb{K}_{i}],\text{ if }\tau i=i\in\mathbb{I},$

$\displaystyle B_{j}\mapsto\frac{{\sqrt{q}}}{q-1}[S_{j}],\text{ if }j\notin\mathbb{I}_{\tau},$
$\displaystyle\qquad\qquad\widetilde{k}_{i}\mapsto\sqrt{q}^{\frac{-c_{i,\tau i}}{2}}[\mathbb{K}_{i}],\quad\text{ if }\tau i\neq i\in\mathbb{I}.$

This theorem for diagonal $\imath$ quivers $(Q\sqcup Q,\text{swap})$ specializes to
Bridgeland’s Hall algebra realization of Drinfeld double quantum groups in [17].
The above monomorphism becomes an isomorphism for Dynkin $\imath$ quivers.
Reflection functors on $\imath$ Hall algebras provide a conceptual approach to braid group actions on $\widetilde{\textbf{U}}^{\imath}$ (of quasi-split type); see [48, 52].

7. Relative braid group actions

Let $(\widetilde{\textbf{U}},\widetilde{\textbf{U}}^{\imath})$ be the universal quantum symmetric pair associated to a Satake diagram $(\mathbb{I}=\mathbb{I}_{\bullet}\cup\mathbb{I}_{\circ},\tau)$ . It is shown in [64] that there exists a quasi $K$ -matrix $\widetilde{\Upsilon}$ associated to $(\widetilde{\textbf{U}},\widetilde{\textbf{U}}^{\imath})$ satisfying an intertwining relation like (2.1).
For $i\in\mathbb{I}_{\circ}$ , denote by $\widetilde{\Upsilon}_{i}$ the quasi $K$ -matrix associated to the rank one Satake subdiagram $\mathbb{I}_{\bullet,i}:=\mathbb{I}_{\bullet}\cup\{i,\tau i\}$ in the setting of $(\widetilde{\textbf{U}},\widetilde{\textbf{U}}^{\imath})$ .

Let $W_{\bullet,i}$ be the parabolic subgroup of the Weyl group $W$ of ${\mathfrak{g}}$ generated by $s_{i}$ , for $i\in\mathbb{I}_{\bullet,i}$ , with longest element $w_{\bullet,i}$ . Define $\mathbf{r}_{i}\in W_{\bullet,i}$ by $\mathbf{r}_{i}=w_{\bullet,i}w_{\bullet}$ ; it is clear that $\mathbf{r}_{i}=\mathbf{r}_{\tau i}$ . Recall $\mathbb{I}_{\tau}$ denotes a set of representatives of the $\tau$ -orbits on $\mathbb{I}_{\circ}$ .
The relative Weyl group associated to the symmetric pair is identified with the subgroup ${\boldsymbol{W}}=\langle\mathbf{r}_{i}\mid i\in\mathbb{I}_{\tau}\rangle$ of $W$ . There is a notion of the relative braid group associated to ${\boldsymbol{W}}$ . The existence of such a relative braid group action on an $\imath$ quantum group ${\textbf{U}}^{\imath}$ was conjectured in [37]. The conjecture was verified therein via compute computation for (mostly quasi-split) finite type; for an alternative approach via $\imath$ Hall algebras see [48, 52].

There is a braid group action associated to $W$ on the Drinfeld double $\widetilde{\textbf{U}}$ (see [52]), a variant of the braid group action on U in [55]. We shall need a suitably rescaled variant, denote by $\widetilde{\mathcal{T}}_{i}^{-1}$ , for $i\in\mathbb{I}$ , which again satisfies the braid group relations. In particular, an automorphism $\widetilde{\mathcal{T}}_{\mathbf{r}_{i}}^{-1}$ of $\widetilde{\textbf{U}}$ , for $i\in\mathbb{I}_{\tau}$ , is defined. We announce a new conceptual approach developed with W. Zhang to relative braid group actions.

paper.title: Quantum symmetric pairs
paper.abstract: This is a survey of some recent progress on quantum symmetric pairs and applications. The topics include quasi K-matrices, $\imath$Schur duality, canonical bases, super Kazhdan-Lusztig theory, $\imath$Hall algebras, current presentations for affine $\imath$quantum groups, and braid group actions.
